distinguishing_features: Uses focused ultrasound radiation pressure and cavitation micro-shockwaves to lower the ice nucleation kinetic barrier within droplet bulk, rather than any valve modulation, current/pressure inference, or operating-envelope restriction
On-demand sononucleation triggered by OAT/static-pressure gating replaces passive heterogeneous nucleation on foreign ice nuclei
Targets the marginal-supercooling regime (-3 to -5 C) where passive AgI seeding fails, via acoustic cavitation rather than consumable seeding agents
Eliminates consumable seed material by shifting from chemical flares to capital HIFU transducer hardware
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to reliably initiate ice nucleation in supercooled cloud droplets at marginal supercooling (warmer than about -5 C) where passive heterogeneous nucleation on foreign nuclei is inefficient, without consuming chemical seeding agents.
parsed.viable_reason: The physics is implausible as written: cavitation requires the local liquid pressure to drop below vapor pressure, but the transducer is mounted on the aircraft fuselage and cannot couple sufficient acoustic intensity into dispersed airborne droplets at 10,000 m, and the stated P_min ~ 0.5*P_stat and 76.5 kPa figures do not establish cavitation in free-falling droplets, making the mechanism infeasible/untestable at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art involves acoustic cavitation for ice nucleation, so applying HIFU sononucleation to marginal-supercooling cloud seeding is not a routine parameter change of the closest art and would not be an obvious step to a skilled engineer.
